subject.title: Output sanitizer: improve duplicate detection for same-line and partial duplicates

question: Should core duplicate sanitization be limited to deterministic exact/tag-boundary artifacts, or should it also remove punctuation-insensitive and partial repeated text?
rationale: The concrete final-tag case is safely repairable, but broader fuzzy matching changes legitimate user-visible content and cannot be selected from source evidence alone.

options.title: Bound deterministic cleanup
options.body: Repair exact glued tag-boundary and narrowly defined adjacent duplicates while explicitly preserving intentional and structurally meaningful repetition.

options.title: Adopt broad fuzzy deduplication
options.body: Permit punctuation-insensitive or partial substring removal and require a larger multilingual and formatting regression matrix before implementation.

options.title: Consolidate under the broad draft
options.body: Pause a separate repair and require https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/68986 to absorb the concrete final-tag case with a narrower reviewed delivery contract.

recommendation.title: Bound deterministic cleanup
recommendation.body: Repair exact glued tag-boundary and narrowly defined adjacent duplicates while explicitly preserving intentional and structurally meaningful repetition.

likelyOwner.reason: The history and prior issue discussion connect this person most directly to the existing sanitizer semantics and the decision about acceptable content-removal heuristics.
